title: Time interval API operations, updates and activation

prose.text: {{operations}} {{list-params}} The other object, time windows, is in [[zia.time-intervals.time-windows]]. Paging behavior of the Go SDK list calls is in [[shared.sdk-go.list-pagination]]. {{go-name-lookup}}

prose.label: Updates.
prose.text: {{update-is-put}} The API response to a partial PUT is gap `omitted-field-on-put`, the same open question as [[zia.sdk-go.write-encoding]] raises for rules.

prose.label: Activation.
prose.text: {{activation-needed}} {{session-end-activates}} The Terraform provider's own activation behavior is in [[zia.terraform.activation]].

checks.do: Whether a delay is relied on as a safety boundary, since a session ending activates pending interval writes.

operations.statement: Time intervals have list, add, get, update and delete operations: GET and POST `/timeIntervals`, and GET, PUT and DELETE `/timeIntervals/{Id}`. The specification lists no `/timeIntervals/lite` path.

update-is-put.statement: Update is a PUT to `/timeIntervals/{Id}`, and the MCP update tool describes it as a PUT-replace that backfills omitted fields from the existing record before sending, so a caller using the SDK directly should send the whole object.

quotes: Update a ZIA time interval (PUT-replace; backfills omitted fields). Activate after.

go-name-lookup.statement: The Go SDK looks up an interval by name by listing every interval and matching case-insensitively.

session-end-activates.statement: ZIA activates pending changes automatically when an API session ends (session timeout of 5 to 20 minutes, default 5) or an admin logs out, so a time interval write staged by the API can go live before it is explicitly activated.

quotes: Pending changes are activated automatically when a session ends
It accepts **5 to 20 minutes and defaults to 5**.

activation-needed.statement: The MCP create and update tools label time interval writes "Activate after", so treat interval changes as staged until activation.

quotes: """Create a ZIA time interval (write). Activate after."""

omitted-field-on-put.title: Whether a PUT that omits a field clears it on a time interval
omitted-field-on-put.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "any field not sent is dropped rather than left untouched." The MCP tool backfills omitted fields, which suggests the concern, but no source shows the API response to a partial PUT. The general question for ZIA rule updates is open in zia.sdk-go.write-encoding.
